title: Customer Escalation: Streaming Response Deadlock -> Idempotent Handoff & Fast-Fail Patch
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers reported sustained 'in-progress' streaming requests that never completed but also never triggered server-side timeouts, causing long-lived resource holds, KV cache pressure, and a wave of client retries that amplified into 5xx spikes for several tenants. This ticket tracks triage, targeted hotfix, and safe rollback plan.

Observed behavior: A subset of streaming sessions (especially multipart streaming with intermittent client reads) entered a state where the server's streaming write loop blocked on a stalled network write or internal buffer flush. Because the request appeared inflight, request-level SLO timers didn't cancel the work; idempotency tokens were absent for these uploads, so retries from SDKs created duplicate concurrent work. The combined effect was prolonged GPU runtime reservations, KV cache thrashing (syncs delayed), and downstream RPC fanout leading to transient 502/504 and application-level timeouts.

Impact: High — several enterprise customers saw degraded throughput and increased latency for chat/streaming flows during the incident window. Some customers filed escalations requesting mitigation and root cause analysis.
steps_taken: 2026-03-10 09:12 — Triage call with oncall, Eng, and SE; captured heap/connection stats and tenant heatmap.
Collected server traces showing stalled epoll writes and incremental build-up of pending KV cache syncs.
Applied emergency mitigation: temporary per-tenant concurrent-stream cap (config flag) to limit resource hogging.
Instrumented additional tracing around streaming write paths and SDK read behavior to better correlate client read stalls with server-side holds.
proposed_fix: Short-term (hotfix): add streaming watchdog that enforces a configurable stall timeout for server write progress. When triggered, perform an idempotent fast-fail with a machine-readable reason and an idempotency handoff token for client-side replay.

Medium-term: extend idempotency model to streaming endpoints — generate session IDs and accept 'handoff' requests that can safely resume or abort prior inflight work without duplicating expensive GPU allocations.
Server change: add non-blocking flush path and backpressure signal to upstream RPCs so stalled downstream connections don't hold critical GPU work open.
SDK change: include keepalive/read-heartbeat guidance and surface fast-fail codes that recommend replay using the handoff token. Update JS/Go SDKs in next minor release.
Operational change: add metric and alarm for 'streaming-stall-count' and a per-tenant reservation gauge to drive automated admission control.
rollout_plan: Build hotfix branch and run CI + integration tests against synthetic streaming harness.
Canary rollout to low-traffic region (us-west-2) with 5% of Hosted traffic for 24h, monitor streaming-stall-count, per-tenant GPU-reservations, and 5xx-rate.
If stable, expand to 25% for additional 48h, then global rollout with staged waves and a scheduled maintenance window for Dedicated/Private customers if required.
Provide opt-out config for Dedicated/Private customers with clear compatibility notes — backport to runtime-1.19 and provide patch instructions for air-gapped installs.
test_plan: Unit tests for new watchdog timer, idempotency token lifecycle, and handoff path.
Integration tests using synthetic clients that simulate intermittent reads, partial TLS writes, and chaotic network pauses.
Load test in staging with KV-cache-heavy workloads to ensure no regression in compaction/eviction under the new fast-fail path.
Chaos test: randomly pause read loops on client to validate graceful degradation and no resource leaks.
postmortem_actions: Post-deploy 1-week monitoring window and automated runbook to disable feature if stall regressions detected.
Document new streaming SLOs and update runbooks for SE/customer support to interpret fast-fail + handoff responses.
Add guided SDK examples in docs showing how to replay with a handoff token and best-effort resume patterns.
Follow-up ticket(s) to evaluate kernel-level socket tuning and further reduce probability of stalled writes under high load.
